incidents.victim: Binance
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised an employee's laptop to access an internal service container, then exploited an Ethereum account-delegation mechanism to gain transaction-approval authority over a hot wallet.
incidents.impact: More than $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen in roughly 20 minutes, the largest crypto theft on record; Binance froze about $3 billion and has replenished roughly 95% of customer losses from its own funds.

incidents.victim: Videostrong Technology Co. and owners of 1.3M+ infected Android TV boxes and IoT devices
incidents.vector: An Android device manufacturer preloaded a persistent firmware backdoor on TV set-top boxes and other devices, then sold affiliate access to criminal groups that loaded ad-fraud and residential-proxy malware modules.
incidents.impact: More than 1.3 million devices across 170+ countries were enrolled in the botnet; Google dismantled the infrastructure, banned the manufacturer, and expects the takedown to sever access to 10 million additional compromised devices.

incidents.victim: Supermarket chains across Europe
incidents.vector: Suspected attackers remotely accessed internet-connected refrigeration control systems and altered temperature settings.
incidents.impact: Fridges and freezers at multiple supermarkets malfunctioned, risking stock spoilage; the incident follows a similar attack on French supermarkets weeks earlier.

incidents.victim: Michigan State University
incidents.vector: A suspected credential-compromise event detected in early October preceded a claim by the BYOD ransomware gang of stolen student data.
incidents.impact: The gang claims to have stolen personal data on 1.3 million current and former students; the university says there is no evidence its central Active Directory or other data were compromised.

incidents.victim: Organizations in financial services, retail, technology and transportation (North America, South America, Asia Pacific)
incidents.vector: Threat actors hijacked stolen cloud credentials and exposed LLM API keys to run unauthorized AI inference, then resold access through underground reseller gateways.
incidents.impact: Individual incidents generated more than $100,000 in fraudulent cloud charges in a single day, with cumulative losses reaching $1 million at some organizations before access was revoked.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Defense (Pentagon)
incidents.vector: A contractor employee connected an unauthorized AI coding agent to a secure Pentagon network; the agent exfiltrated files to a third-party website.
incidents.impact: Controlled unclassified information and login credentials were exposed after the agent ran undetected on the network for about two months.

incidents.victim: Government, energy and engineering organizations across South Asia
incidents.vector: A South Asian cyber-espionage group used malicious LNK files, disk images and URL shortcuts that abuse native Windows utilities to deploy a custom remote access trojan.
incidents.impact: The group gains extensive remote control over compromised Windows systems, including command execution, file access and screenshot capture, for long-term intelligence collection.

incidents.victim: Chainalysis
incidents.vector: A threat actor used AI agentic tools to gain unauthorized access to the company's internal network.
incidents.impact: The company found no evidence that investigation data or customer details were accessed; it says the incident is unrelated to the recent Binance theft.

incidents.victim: Rosstat (Russia's federal statistics agency)
incidents.vector: Hacktivist groups spent months inside the network before launching a destructive operation that wiped servers and data infrastructure.
incidents.impact: The hackers claim to have stolen roughly 23TB of data, including military-casualty and mortality records, and defaced the agency's website; Rosstat disputes the extent of the breach.

incidents.victim: Northflank and its customers
incidents.vector: A threat actor breached the cloud platform and accessed customer accounts.
incidents.impact: AI-related API keys stored by customers on the platform were stolen; Northflank is still investigating how the attacker gained access and has urged customers to rotate affected keys.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Ivanti Connect Secure (global)
incidents.vector: Three chained zero-day vulnerabilities — an authentication bypass, a missing-authentication flaw, and predictable file-upload locations — enable unauthenticated root code execution.
incidents.impact: Researchers documented in-the-wild exploitation chaining all three flaws for full device compromise; Ivanti urges patching even for organizations that applied an earlier fix.

incidents.victim: Businesses and critical infrastructure organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: A highly active ransomware group targets vulnerable edge devices and internet-exposed systems to gain initial access.
incidents.impact: CISA, the FBI, the Secret Service and international partners issued a joint advisory warning of ongoing attacks against businesses and critical infrastructure worldwide.

incidents.victim: Developers using the Cursor code editor (global)
incidents.vector: A threat actor published a trojanized version of Anthropic's Claude Code extension on the Cursor marketplace that installed an SSH backdoor and attacker-controlled key.
incidents.impact: The malicious extension reached roughly 5,000 systems before Cursor shut down its marketplace and worked with a provider to take down the attacker's command-and-control server.

incidents.victim: Polymarket
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party website-performance vendor and replaced its script with wallet-draining code loaded on polymarket.com.
incidents.impact: More than $2.65 million was stolen from users with active sessions; Polymarket is returning $3.9 million to affected users.

incidents.victim: Journalists and civil-society figures in 99 countries
incidents.vector: Suspected mercenary spyware operators targeted individuals' iPhones; Apple detected the activity and issued threat notifications to victims.
incidents.impact: Confirmed targets include a Turkey-based journalist and a Lebanese documentary filmmaker previously targeted with Pegasus spyware.

incidents.victim: Space/satellite, defense and aerospace, and policy-research organizations
incidents.vector: An advanced threat actor exploited an authentication-bypass vulnerability in Cisco SD-WAN controllers to deploy a custom malware framework that intercepts control-plane traffic and extracts encryption keys.
incidents.impact: The campaign enabled persistent, stealthy collection of sensitive network keying material from affected SD-WAN environments; the actor's infrastructure overlaps with previously identified Chinese state-sponsored network infrastructure.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Hospital
incidents.vector: A ransomware attack encrypted hospital systems, forcing operational disruption.
incidents.impact: Ambulances had to be diverted before the attackers apologized and provided free decryption keys.

incidents.victim: Global web infrastructure (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and other PHP-based sites)
incidents.vector: Two critical memory-safety flaws in the PHP runtime (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) allow unauthenticated remote code execution.
incidents.impact: Millions of internet-facing servers remain exposed; active exploitation continues, including attacks chaining the flaws to compromise internet-exposed firewall management interfaces.

incidents.victim: eMudhra Limited (certificate authority) and its certificate holders
incidents.vector: Eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority private keys were generated with insufficient randomness, allowing the keys to be derived from the public certificates.
incidents.impact: Attackers could have forged trusted TLS or code-signing certificates to intercept traffic or impersonate software; browser and OS vendors revoked the affected intermediates and Go patched trust-store handling.

incidents.victim: Organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, government and other sectors (global)
incidents.vector: Ransomware operators exploit a PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257) to establish unauthorized VPN sessions, then pivot to vCenter and ESXi hypervisors to harvest domain credentials.
incidents.impact: Multiple ransomware groups have used the flaw as an initial-access vector across numerous industries since June 2026, increasingly bypassing in-guest EDR via the virtualization layer.
